moat_against: Structurally low-growth categories; private label takes share when budgets tighten
P&G is a larger, stronger rival in the core categories
Organic growth currently minimal — Q2 2026 sales +0.6%, organic roughly flat
China diaper social-media crisis cut ~140bp from Q2 organic growth and forced a guidance cut
Growth increasingly deal-bought (Kenvue) rather than organic, with integration/leverage risk
moat_for: Iconic brands (Huggies, Kleenex, Scott, Kotex, Depend) with decades of shelf presence and retailer scale
Proven pricing power — 2023 organic sales +5% driven by ~+6% price
Essential, non-cyclical demand in diapers, tissue and personal care
Scale economies in pulp purchasing, manufacturing and distribution
10th straight quarter of volume growth reported in Q2 2026
moat_justification: Genuine brand equity and shelf scale with demonstrated pricing power (2023 organic +5% on ~+6% price), but categories are structurally low-growth, private label caps pricing, P&G contests every core category, organic growth is currently flat (Q2 2026 organic ~0%, H1 +1.2%), and growth is increasingly deal-bought (Kenvue) with integration and leverage risk.
name: Kimberly-Clark Corporation
one_liner: Durable brand staple, moat 6/10 — but at $98.36 the TTM OE yield is only 5.15% and even the super-bull path reaches just 11.53% IRR; Tier D, weighted IRR 7.78%, weighted IV@15% $41.46 — clears the 15% hurdle only near $41.
